title: Radar range and velocity
target: Separate a radar’s range measurement from its line-of-sight velocity measurement.
criteria: Explain the information in a Doppler shift.
State what radial velocity leaves unknown.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A radar echo returns in 8.0 microseconds. Use c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. What is one-way range to a stationary target?
cpa.guide: Total path is cΔt = 2,400 m; range is half.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A scaled signal model has speed 32 m/s and echo delay 5.0 s. What is target range?
cpa.guide: Range = vΔt/2 = 32 × 5 / 2 = 80 m. This is a scaled model, not real radar speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A reflected radar signal has a Doppler shift consistent with approach. What quantity does this primarily constrain?
options: The object’s mass directly.
The component of relative velocity along the radar line of sight.
Its exact shape regardless of other data.
Its full three-dimensional velocity from one shift alone.
cpa.guide: Doppler measures radial relative motion, not every component.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two targets at different ranges have the same radial approach speed. Under otherwise identical simple radar conditions, which statement is possible?
options: Echo delay alone gives both masses.
They have the same Doppler shift but different echo delays.
The more distant target must have zero Doppler shift.
Equal Doppler shift requires equal distance.
cpa.guide: Delay measures range; Doppler constrains radial velocity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A target moves sideways at an instant, perpendicular to a radar’s line of sight. Can near-zero radial speed mean the target is motionless?
options: Yes; all motion must be toward the radar.
Yes; radial and total speed are always identical.
No; transverse motion can still be substantial.
No; it proves the target moves at light speed.
cpa.guide: A single radial component does not determine transverse components.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A single radar measures range and radial velocity. What additional evidence helps determine a full path?
options: The radar’s paint color.
Assuming sideways speed is zero without evidence.
Measurements over time or from other viewing directions.
Only a stronger claim based on the same instant.
cpa.guide: Additional geometry and timing constrain otherwise unknown motion components.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.
